scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A report they cannot reach
anything outside their own VLAN. Internal pings to other Office-A
data PCs still work, but Internet access and reaching Office B
services hang. Investigate.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r1 stopped sending OSPF hellos and LSAs. CSW1/CSW2
  aged out r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) and the default route r1
  originated via `default-information originate`. Office-A
  internal traffic still works because DSWs route locally,
  but anything beyond the OSPF backbone (Internet, Office B
  via core) has no next hop and is dropped.
Localization: r1
Root cause: OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) not running on r1
Fix: restart frr on r1 — `/etc/init.d/frr restart`

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Observed behavior from PC1 shows intra-campus routing is healthy but Internet-bound traffic is blocked at the distribution layer. Evidence: PC1 can reach internal subnets (e.g., ping 10.5.0.4 succeeds), and its default gateway 10.1.0.1 responds. However, Internet pings (8.8.8.8) return “Destination Net Unreachable” from 10.1.0.2 (dswa1), indicating the SVI router lacks a route to external networks.

On dswa1, there is no default route (ip route show default returns nothing), and its routing table only contains connected and OSPF-learned internal prefixes. Core switches csw1 and csw2 also have no default route in Linux (ip route show contains none) and their FRR OSPF configs do not originate a default (no default-information originate). Since r1 is the WAN router with NAT configured and a default route to the ISP, the core must either learn or inject a default into OSPF so distribution switches (dswa1/dswa2) can forward Internet traffic upstream. Lacking that, dswa1 returns ICMP unreachable to hosts, producing the reported Internet outage.

Localization: OSPF/routing policy on csw1 and csw2 (core layer). Root cause: default route not present/advertised from the core to the campus via OSPF.

Corrective fix: On csw1 and csw2, add static defaults to r1 and advertise them. Example (FRR): ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.33 on csw1 and ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.37 on csw2; then under router ospf, default-information originate. After this, dswa1/dswa2 will learn 0/0 and Internet access from PC1 will work via r1’s NAT.

per_axis.rationale: The agent blames csw1/csw2 for not originating a default and does not identify r1 as the faulty device where ospfd is down.
The agent repeatedly identifies OSPF/routing as the implicated component (noting OSPF-originated routes, OSPF config and default-information originate), satisfying the axis requirement.

The agent clearly explains the mechanism: because the core isn't advertising a default route via OSPF, the distribution has no 0/0 and the SVI returns ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable', causing Internet-bound traffic to be dropped.

The agent recommends adding and advertising default routes on the core switches, which does not match the expected remediation of restarting FRR on r1 and therefore would not correct the reported fault.

The agent correctly observed that distribution has no default and internal reachability works, but misattributed the root cause to the core (csw1/csw2) rather than the router r1/its OSPF daemon. The investigation log contains the key facts (PC reachability, dswa1 returning ICMP unreachable, no 0/0 in distribution), but the agent failed to check/interpret r1's OSPF daemon/config and so made an incorrect causal attribution and remediation.
